reasons: The rule's preferred position is the absence of any non-solicit binding the Customer; the cited transition provisions (Sections 7.4/7.5) impose only cooperation and records/funds-transfer duties and contain no solicit/hire/induce covenant, so 'compliant' is the correct classification.
Consistent with a compliant finding, no redline was proposed and no comment was added — the rendered text is identical to the original paragraphs, which is the expected output.
The failed deterministic checks (duration ≤ 12 months, general-solicitation carve-out) are artifacts of there being no non-solicit clause to measure; they do not indicate a substantive defect here.

Cited paragraphs are relevant evidence of absence (post-termination transition duties are the most likely home for such a covenant), and the rationale accurately notes the proprietary-process carve-out does not restrict hiring of Servicer personnel.
